Dimorphos’s orbit around the larger asteroid Didymos kept changing in the weeks after DART’s impact.

Before the impact, an orbit took 11 hours and 55 minutes. Immediately afterward, the period was shorter. Over the following weeks, it shortened further. During that same period, Dimorphos also lost more rocky material to space.

The orbit eventually settled at 11 hours and 22 minutes—about 33 minutes shorter than before—and was no longer circular. The orbital change continued well beyond the immediate aftermath of the impact.
